record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Let p1, ..., pℓ be an intersective family of integer polynomials, meaning that for every positive integer r there exists n with p_i(n) divisible by r for all i. For every commuting measure-preserving system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and every measurable A with μ(A) > 0, must there exist n such that μ(A ∩ T1^{p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}A) > 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Let (X, X , µ, T1, . . . , T`) be a system and {p1, . . . , p`} be a family of intersective integer polynomials. Show that for every set A ∈ X with µ(A) > 0 one has µ(A ∩ T1^p1(n)A ∩ · · · ∩ T`^p`(n)A) > 0 for some n ∈ N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\ell \geq 1$ and let $p_1, \dots, p_\ell \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a jointly intersective family of integer polynomials, meaning that for every positive integer $r$ there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $r \mid p_i(n)$ for all $i = 1, \dots, \ell$. Let $(X, \mathcal{X}, \mu, T_1, \dots, T_\ell)$ be a measure-preserving system, where $(X, \mathcal{X}, \mu)$ is a probability space and $T_1, \dots, T_\ell$ are commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of $X$. Prove or disprove: for every $A \in \mathcal{X}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$ there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A \cap T_1^{p_1(n)} A \cap T_2^{p_2(n)} A \cap \cdots \cap T_\ell^{p_\ell(n)} A\bigr) > 0.$$
artifact.category_tag: multiple ergodic averages and polynomial recurrence
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of multiple recurrence for jointly intersective polynomial families and commuting measure-preserving transformations appears to remain open. Substantial recent progress (e.g., joint ergodicity results for commuting transformations published in Inventiones 2024 by Frantzikinakis–Kuca, and partial results for rationally independent or single-transformation cases via Bergelson–Leibman) addresses important special cases but does not resolve the fully general intersective-polynomial recurrence problem for arbitrary commuting systems.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity for commuting transformations and applications to polynomial sequences
status_evidence.snippet: necessary and sufficient conditions for joint ergodicity results of collections of sequences with respect to systems of commuting measure preserving transformations
status_evidence.claim: Recent results settle joint ergodicity for commuting transformations with polynomial iterates, but the general intersective recurrence problem is broader.

status_evidence.title: Intersective polynomials and the polynomial Szemerédi theorem
status_evidence.snippet: A polynomial family has the PSZ property if and only if the polynomials are jointly intersective.
status_evidence.claim: The single-transformation case (T_1=...=T_l) is known to be equivalent to joint intersectivity (Bergelson–Leibman–Lesigne).

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence for non-commuting transformations along rationally independent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: the question whether a similar recurrence result for non-commuting transformations holds for rationally dependent polynomials remains open
status_evidence.claim: Related recurrence questions for general polynomial families remain open.
